cultivar: Assam bush (Camellia sinensis var. assamica) seedlings and clones
processing: Freshly plucked assamica leaf is steamed or pan-fired to prevent oxidation, rolled and dried; a small side line at orthodox gardens and organic small growers.
harvest_season: Spring to autumn; the first flush (March–April) is the gentlest, later lots are coarser.
appearance_dry: Dark green, loosely twisted, somewhat coarse leaf.
taste_profile: Bold for a green tea: vegetal and lightly malty with a brisk, drying finish and a touch of honey when brewed cool.

brewing.notes: Cool water and short steeps; assamica leaf is rich in catechins and turns bitter fast.

vintage_note: Sold by garden and year, often with an organic certificate, and increasingly by small-grower cooperatives; drink within the year of harvest. Most Assam green goes to the Indian domestic health-tea market, so it is cheap at home and a curiosity abroad, with no vintage or aged market.
description:
Assam green tea is the odd one out in a valley built on strong black tea: the same big-leaved assamica bushes, but fired before the leaf can oxidise. It has been made in small quantities for decades and has grown with India's domestic green-tea boom, mostly from organic small growers and a few orthodox estates.

Fresh leaf is steamed or pan-fired to stop oxidation, rolled and dried. Because assamica leaf is large and rich in catechins, the result is a bolder, more astringent green than Chinary leaf gives, with a dark olive look and a yellow-amber cup.

Brewed cool it shows a mild honeyed sweetness and a faint malty note under the vegetal character, with a brisk, drying finish; brewed hot it turns bitter very quickly. Keep the water at around 80 °C and the steeps short, and treat it more like a hearty Chinese green than a Japanese one.

It is sold by garden and year, often with an organic certificate, and the first flush in March and April is the gentlest. Most of it is sold within India as a health tea, so abroad it is a curiosity found at a few importers rather than a staple. Buy the current year's lot and use it within the year.

Worth a try if you like strong greens, or if you want to taste the raw material of Assam black tea before oxidation.
